title: Canadian PM Carney Dismisses Trump Adviser's 'Get the Hell Out' Remarks to Lobbyists
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed remarks by a Trump adviser telling Canadian lobbyists to 'get the hell out' of the United States, underscoring continued friction in the US-Canada relationship amid ongoing trade tensions.

title: Navarro Pushes Broad Tariff Overhaul Targeting US Allies
detail: Trump trade adviser Peter Navarro is pushing a broad tariff overhaul extending to US allies, signaling the administration intends to expand its trade restructuring agenda beyond adversaries. The move signals escalating trade pressure even on traditional partners.

title: Section 301 Forced-Labor Tariffs on 60 Countries Face Legal Challenge at US Court of International Trade
detail: Trump's Section 301 forced-labor tariffs targeting 60 countries are under legal challenge at the US Court of International Trade, with a hearing now underway. The tariffs were part of the administration's broad trade restructuring agenda aimed at eliminating forced-labor imports.

title: Canadian PM Carney Vows Stelco's US Owner Will Face 'Fullest Extent of the Law' Over Sudden Layoffs
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney warned that Stelco's US owner will face the 'fullest extent of the law' following sudden layoffs at the steelmaker linked to trade-related plant decisions. The development adds to trade friction between Canada and the US.

title: Trump State Department Diverts Human Rights Funds to Promote Far-Right Agenda Abroad
detail: A Guardian investigation found that the Trump State Department has diverted funds originally designated for human rights programs to instead promote a far-right agenda in foreign countries. The move represents a significant shift in US foreign policy priorities under Secretary of State Rubio.

title: Trump Ally Urges Administration to 'Step Back' and Rethink Immigration Agenda Amid Internal Pushback
detail: A prominent Trump ally publicly urged the administration to 'step back' and reconsider its immigration agenda, citing growing internal pushback. The call to pause reflects mounting concerns within Trump's own circle about the pace and scope of the administration's immigration enforcement drive.
